key_insight: World models—latent generative models that simulate dynamics and counterfactuals—can unify epidemiological state inference, policy-dependent observation modeling, and behavior-mediated intervention effects, enabling better planning under uncertainty.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in computational epidemiology for jointly reasoning about unobserved disease burden, imperfect and policy-dependent surveillance signals, and how interventions interact with adaptive human behavior to affect outcomes.
method: Learn a latent-state world model that encodes hidden epidemic dynamics and ties them to noisy, policy-dependent surveillance observations.
Use the learned simulator to generate counterfactual futures under different interventions and behavioral responses for planning and evaluation.
Incorporate policy-conditioned observation models and behavior modules so interventions and surveillance adaptively influence simulated signals and outcomes.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical modeling paradigm to build more realistic, testable epidemiological simulators for decision support, bridging representation learning, causal counterfactuals, and policy-aware surveillance modeling.
visual_elements: Schematic of a world-model loop: latent epidemic state → simulator (interventions & behavior) → observation model → inference update
Counterfactual timeline chart comparing epidemic trajectories under alternative interventions
Icon set showing data sources (tests, hospitalizations, mobility) with arrows indicating policy-dependent noise
Heatmap or uncertainty band visualization illustrating model uncertainty across simulated futures
paper_authors: Zeeshan Memon, Yiqi Su, Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Walid Saad, Liang Zhao
